title: Nonzero maps of line bundles give a nonnegative tensor-dual degree difference
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $C$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $A,B$ be invertible $\mathcal O_C$-modules and put $A^\vee=\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_C}(A,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and $L=B\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}A^\vee$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Both $A^\vee$ and $L$ are invertible. There is a canonical $\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)$-linear isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_C}(A,B)\simeq\Gamma(C,L)$$
which sends a morphism $\varphi$ locally given by $\varphi(e_A)=h e_B$, for local bases $e_A,e_B$, to the section locally given by $h e_B\otimes e_A^\vee$. For $\varphi\ne0$ its corresponding global section $s_\varphi$ is nonzero. Evaluation is an isomorphism $A\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}A^\vee\simeq\mathcal O_C$. With $\deg_k N=\chi(C,N)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)\in\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], [def-pc-euler-characteristic], one has
$$\deg_k A^\vee=-\deg_k A,\qquad \deg_k L=\deg_k B-\deg_k A.$$
If $\varphi\ne0$, then $\deg_k L\ge0$.

source.place: Tag 0B40 (varieties-lemma-check-invertible-sheaf-trivial), proof of (5) via (1), including the displayed sheaf Hom identity; Tag 0AYX (varieties-lemma-degree-tensor-product), rank-one case.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible] to $A$ and $B$: $A^\vee$ is invertible, $L=B\otimes A^\vee$ is invertible, and the canonical evaluation $A\otimes A^\vee\to\mathcal O_C$ is an isomorphism.

Choose a common Zariski trivializing cover for $A,B$ using [def-sc-invertible-module]. On a member with bases $e_A,e_B$, send $\varphi(e_A)=h e_B$ to $h e_B\otimes e_A^\vee$. If $e_A'=u e_A$ and $e_B'=v e_B$ on an overlap, with $u,v$ units, then $h'=uv^{-1}h$ and $(e_A')^\vee=u^{-1}e_A^\vee$, so $h'e_B'\otimes(e_A')^\vee=h e_B\otimes e_A^\vee$. Thus these local sections glue. Conversely a section locally written $h e_B\otimes e_A^\vee$ gives the maps $e_A\mapsto h e_B$; the same formula makes them agree on overlaps. These constructions commute with restrictions, addition and multiplication by functions, and are inverse on each trivializing open. Hence they give the asserted canonical $\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)$-linear isomorphism. Zero corresponds locally to $h=0$, so $s_\varphi=0$ if and only if $\varphi=0$.

source.place: Tag 0B40, varieties-lemma-check-invertible-sheaf-trivial, proof of (5): the sheaf Hom identity and application of (1).

proof.text: By [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], $\deg_k\mathcal O_C=\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)=0$. Apply [lem-trf-curve-degree-tensor-additive] to $A,A^\vee$; evaluation from Step 1 identifies their tensor product with $\mathcal O_C$. The evaluation isomorphism and its inverse induce inverse $k$-linear maps on every $H^i(C,-)$; hence the dimensions in [def-pc-euler-characteristic] agree term by term, giving equal Euler characteristics and degrees. Thus $0=\deg_k A+\deg_k A^\vee$. Thus $\deg_k A^\vee=-\deg_k A$. Apply the same tensor formula to $B,A^\vee$ to obtain $\deg_k L=\deg_k B-\deg_k A$. The dimension-one hypothesis implies dimension at most one, as required by that formula.

source.place: Tag 0AYX, varieties-lemma-degree-tensor-product, rank-one case; Tag 0B40, proof of (5), degree of the tensor-dual bundle.

proof.text: If $\varphi\ne0$, Step 2 supplies the nonzero section $s_\varphi$ of the invertible bundle $L$. Apply [lem-trf-curve-section-degree-positivity] to $(C,L,s_\varphi)$. Its hypotheses are exactly that $C$ is integral, proper over the field $k$, and of dimension one; it yields $\deg_k L\ge0$.
